text:
Jordan: Heads up — since the RBAC refactor we pushed last night, multiple customer SSO logins are getting mapped to `Viewer` instead of Owner/Editor. Seeing SAML assertion where `groups` claim is empty. Anyone else seeing this?
Prasanna: Yep, noticed a spike in `role_mismatch` events around 22:05 UTC for prod-okta-app. Digging into SAML payloads now.
Kevin: Can you paste an example assertion (scrubbed)?
Prasanna: Here's a scrubbed example we got from the access logs:
```xml
<saml:Assertion>
  <saml:AttributeStatement>
    <saml:Attribute Name="appRole">
      <saml:AttributeValue></saml:AttributeValue>
    </saml:Attribute>
    <saml:Attribute Name="groups">
      <saml:AttributeValue></saml:AttributeValue>
    </saml:Attribute>
  </saml:AttributeStatement>
</saml:Assertion>
```
Prasanna: Looks like Okta started sending empty values for both `appRole` and `groups` for some accounts. I traced it — the Okta mapping we use was overwritten by an admin change earlier today.
Leo: Wasn't the plan for our consumer to fallback to `groups` if `appRole` was missing? I thought the refactor removed some of that logic.
Prasanna: Correct — during the RBAC refactor we tightened attribute expectations and removed the legacy fallback to groups to simplify role inference. That made the consumer strict; now when `appRole` is empty we default to `Viewer`.
Jordan: Who changed the Okta mapping? We need cause + fix.
Kevin: Okta admin audit shows a manual edit: `vendor-svc@partner.com` changed app attribute mapping at 2026-03-19T22:04:12Z. That coincides with the failure window.
Prasanna: Quick mitigation: I created a temporary mapping in Okta to map group membership -> `appRole` for the affected app (rule: `Groups -> appRole`), and re-enabled JIT fallback for existing users. Rolling that to all prod tenants now.
devops-bot: deploy job `okta-map-rollout-42` succeeded — change applied to prod 3 regions.
Jordan: Thanks. Can we also revert consumer behavior to be more tolerant until we finish the refactor? Falling back to `groups` is safer.
Prasanna: I opened PR #3942 to reintroduce a tolerant parsing path (if `appRole` empty then use `groups` claim). Also added unit + integration tests against mocked Okta assertions.
Kevin: We should add an audit event whenever we apply a fallback so compliance can track when user roles aren't determined solely by primary attribute.
Prasanna: Agreed — adding an `rbac.fallback_used` audit event. We should ensure it is safe to store and that we don't write any secrets. Might wrap the audit entry with KMS envelope if needed for integrity.
Leo: For the short term, assign @Leo to own the Okta mapping runbook and validate admin change controls.
Leo: Taking it. I'll add a checklist for mapping edits (owners, approval, test tenant validation).
Jordan: Also put an alert on `role_mismatch` rate and a pager for > 10/min for high-severity customers. I added the monitor.
Kevin: Filing post-incident actions: ticket INC-2341 created, linking PR #3942 and Okta audit.
Prasanna: Follow-ups: 1) Merge tolerant parsing PR 2) Add `rbac.fallback_used` audit event (ensure KMS/HSM integrity if required by compliance) 3) Add Okta admin change guardrails + runbook 4) Add e2e tests for SAML attribute permutations.
Jordan: Good. One more compliance note — once fallback events exist, we need a report for auditors that shows how often fallback was applied per customer. Add to the quarterly audit plan.
Prasanna: Will do. Closing once PR and alerting are in place.
Jordan: Thanks all. :thumbsup:
